threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 26 bus is reliable. It’s a wild card, like betting on the weather here.
Saw a guy in a parka serenading a sleeping passenger with a ukulele on the 37. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw kids painting a mural on the side of the U-Bahn station while a group of elders argued about the best kebab spot nearby.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a public park where people casually bring their own grill, set up for hours, and no one bats an eye. That’s just a Saturday here.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they know to avoid Civic Center BART during a meltdown. Tourists just stare at the chaos, confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 31 last night doing a magic trick with his phone—swiped left and right, then vanished it. Muni’s stage for real life magic.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think every plaza is for partying, but locals know it’s the kids' playgrounds that keep the real vibe alive, especially in the mornings.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot a recent arrival by their constant phone usage at La Rambla, oblivious to the street musicians right beside them.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the newcomers by their bewildered looks when the Tube strikes hit—like, haven’t they heard this is our second home now?
Last night on the 196, a couple was arguing about whether or not they could fit their takeaway in the overhead rack. It was a tight squeeze, but they made it work.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Walking past the Turkish market on Monday, I spotted a guy haggling over the price of baklava while a hipster juggled coffee cups. Classic Neukölln moment.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a hidden club in a former factory basement, complete with a dance floor that used to be a giant swimming pool.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their reaction to BART delays—rolling their eyes like it’s an old friend. Tourists just look lost and frustrated.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo getting off the 38 Geary, holding a bouquet. Guessing he was late to the wedding, but Muni never cares about your plans.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real charm is in the small plazas where locals sip their café, far from the hustle.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the bewildered looks when they order a 'café con leche' and expect a small cup, not a full glass.
